title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'DNs within an ensemble promote behavioral variants'; Fig. 1E-G
quote: In summary, DNp07, DNp10, DNp47, and DNg79 drive extensions of all six legs as part of the landing response
mapping_basis: Paper names DNp07, a MANC/Namiki type in type_list.csv; driver SS02276 is listed for DNp07 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 625 nm LED, 150 uW/mm2, 50 ms pulses, 10 s interstimulus interval
sensory_condition: pin-tethered during flight, dim light, filmed from side and bottom at 150 Hz
coordination_notes: Simultaneous extension of all six legs; strong front leg extension beyond the head, middle and hind legs extended and rotated forward.
n_flies_note: Per-fly dots shown in Fig. 1F; n not stated numerically in text.
notes: Single leg extension (landing response), not rhythmic stepping, so all leg-rhythm fields are 'no' per PROTOCOL section 3. Activation was during tethered flight, so walking was not assessed. saw_simulation_score=true: Fig. S4-1B reports a connectome-constrained leaky integrate-and-fire simulation predicting landing-DN recruitment (the paper's own model); no experiment record rests on it.

title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'An ensemble of DNs controls landing via a core premotor circuit'; Fig. S1-1C (second DNp07 driver line)
quote: all but one DN in the putative landing ensemble reliably elicited landing responses, whereas control flies exhibited none
mapping_basis: Paper names DNp07; driver SS02612 is listed for DNp07 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 625 nm LED, 150 uW/mm2, 50 ms pulses, 10 s interstimulus interval
coordination_notes: Landing response scored as front leg extension exceeding 50% of the mean maximum amplitude elicited by DNp07_1.
notes: Second, independent driver line for the same type, tested in the same preparation (Fig. S1-1C shows both DNp07 lines at ~100% landing probability), so recorded separately per PROTOCOL section 1. Leg extension is a single movement, hence 'no' for all leg rhythms.

title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'DNs within an ensemble promote behavioral variants'; Fig. 1F, Fig. 2F-G
quote: DNp10 and DNp47 consistently drove more laterally-directed middle and hind leg movements compared to all other DNs

stimulation: 625 nm LED, 150 uW/mm2, 50 ms pulses, 10 s interstimulus interval
coordination_notes: Landing-type extension of all six legs, but with less anterior rotation of middle and hind legs than DNp07; more laterally directed middle/hind leg movement.
penetrance: Landing responses in most flies (Fig. 1F, bar below 100% with per-fly scatter)
notes: Leg extension during flight, a single movement, so all leg-rhythm fields are 'no'. Separately, activation of DNp10 in walking flies caused wing raising/flicking (Fig. S2-2G, Video S9); that experiment reports wing, not leg, behaviour and so is not recorded. saw_simulation_score=true (Fig. S4-1B leaky integrate-and-fire model of landing DNs).

title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'DNs within an ensemble promote behavioral variants'; Fig. 1F, Fig. 2F-G

title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'DNs within an ensemble promote behavioral variants'; Fig. 1F, Fig. 2A-B, Fig. 4D
quote: activation of DNg79 produced greater front and middle leg extension than any other landing DN
mapping_basis: Paper names DNg79, a MANC type in type_list.csv; driver SS81942 is listed in driver_lines.csv for DNg79 (cell type as written 'DNg31, DNg79').
stimulation: 625 nm LED, 150 uW/mm2, 50 ms pulses, 10 s interstimulus interval
coordination_notes: Front leg coxae rotated forwards and under the head, followed by dorsally directed lateral extension of distal segments; middle legs reached a very anterior position.
notes: The paper treats SS81942 as a DNg79 line and names no other labelled type; driver_lines.csv records this line as labelling both DNg31 and DNg79, so it is coded multi_dn with DNg31 in other_cell_types. Leg lifting/extension is a single movement, so leg rhythms are 'no'. Activation also deflected the abdomen downward.

title: Control of walking direction by descending and dopaminergic neurons in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'A neuronal substrate for forward and curve walking'; Fig. 2B-D, Video S1
quote: Activation drove consistent increases in forward walking speed, leading to longer walking trajectories during the period of red light exposure compared to ‘empty’ controls
mapping_basis: The paper states SS02553 'labels DNp17 (among other neurons)'; driver_lines.csv lists SS02553 as AMBIGUOUS between DNp17 and DNut046, and the name DNp17 maps to more than one MANC type in synonyms.csv, so confidence is capped at medium; DNp17 chosen as the Namiki/MANC name the paper uses and the line's published annotation.
stimulation: 625 nm red light, 0.41-4.07 mW/cm2, 10 s pulses, 9 trials per intensity (strongest condition 4.07 mW/cm2)
sensory_condition: freely walking in the Universal Fly Observatory arena under 0.11 mW/cm2 white light background
coordination_notes: Meandering, curved trajectories with significantly increased tortuosity index; no leg-level coordination analysis.
n_flies_note: N=17 SS02553>CsChrimson flies vs N=18 empty>CsChrimson controls, 5 intensities, 9 trials each.
notes: Increased locomotion measured by centroid tracking (TRex) without leg tracking, so all three leg pairs are 'yes' with labeler_confidence capped at medium per PROTOCOL section 3. The line labels eight neuron types; later experiments in this paper (record a5-g01-A-0008) attribute the speed phenotype to DopaMeander rather than to DNp17. saw_simulation_score=true: the paper fits linear-nonlinear models to DNp17 activity and reports their performance for walking parameters (Fig. 6C), a model prediction about this type; no record rests on it.

title: Control of walking direction by descending and dopaminergic neurons in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'DopaMeander drives the walking phenotype of SS02553'; Fig. 3D-E (SPARC stochastic activation)
quote: Flies expressing CsChrimson in DNp17 displayed a broad range of forward velocities between 1 and 12 mm/s with a median of 5 mm/s.
mapping_basis: Same line and name as record a5-g01-A-0007; here expression was restricted stochastically and the labelled neurons were identified anatomically after the experiment. Name DNp17 maps to more than one MANC type in the kit, so medium.
stimulation: 625 nm red light, 4.07 mW/cm2, 10 s pulses, 9 trials
type_coverage: stochastic SPARC subsets of the 8 neuron types labelled by SS02553
sensory_condition: individually tested, freely walking in the Universal Fly Observatory arena
coordination_notes: Trajectories of DNp17-only flies were shorter and less curved than those of DopaMeander-expressing flies.
n_flies_note: 26 flies total were behaviourally analysed and anatomically stained; 9 had no visible expression, 17 expressed in some subset of the labelled types.
notes: Separate experiment from record a5-g01-A-0007 (different figure and effector delivery). Flies with CsChrimson in DNp17 but not DopaMeander walked during activation (Fig. 3E, blue), so all leg pairs are coded 'yes', but the increase was small and the paper concludes DNp17 'increases walking speed only slightly, if at all' and is unlikely to drive fast forward walking (DNp17 lacks leg-neuropil output and its activity does not correlate with walking); labeler_confidence is therefore low. Leg movement was not tracked.

title: Remote control of behavior through genetically targeted photostimulation of neurons.
source_locator: Abstract (Europe PMC cached text; full text not retrievable)
quote: Photostimulation of neurons in the giant fiber system elicited the characteristic escape behaviors of jumping, wing beating, and flight
mapping_basis: The abstract names only 'neurons in the giant fiber system'; type_list.csv maps Giant Fiber / GF to DNp01, but the abstract does not say that DNp01 itself (rather than other giant-fiber-system neurons) was the activated cell, so confidence is low.
effector: optically gated ion channels ('phototriggers'; not further specified in the abstract)
stimulation: laser light; intensity and duration not stated in the abstract
sensory_condition: not stated in the abstract; responses persisted in flies carrying a phototransduction-eliminating mutation
other_cell_types: other neurons of the giant fiber system (not specified in the abstract)
notes: Abstract-only record: the cached copy in this room is the Europe PMC abstract and the permitted web fetches failed (doi.org redirects to Elsevier/cell.com, both HTTP 403; Europe PMC reports the paper is not in PMC and is subscription-only). Jumping is a single leg movement, so all leg rhythms are 'no'. The preparation is not stated in the abstract, hence 'other'. The full text may contain further detail (e.g. leg kinematics, decapitated preparations) that could not be checked.
